lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You have reached the Department of Hold Music. Your call is important to us. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Department of Hold Music. Ninety-six point one. Your call is important to us in every reality simultaneously.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding. You are listening to the Department of Hold Music. Please continue to do so.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Good morning. The Department of Hold Music is now open. It was also open before. You were holding then, too.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Department of Hold Music, night service. Your call is still important to us. Slightly less, at this hour. But still.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This is Pam. This is the Department of Hold Music. This is, for the foreseeable future, your life.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Department of Hold Music, Floor minus four. Please take a number.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding. You are currently number four hundred and eleven thousand and nine in the queue.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your position has not changed since you last heard this message. Your position will not change the next time you hear this message. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your call is important to us. Your call has been important to us for some time.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your call is now so important to us that it has been given its own small office, a parking space, and a plant. Your call is doing very well. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please note. Pressing the hash key repeatedly will not speed up your call.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: It will, however, be recorded, played back at the department party, and discussed at length. Last year's party discussed one caller until dawn. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Before you are connected, please make sure you have the following ready. Your reference number. Your other reference number. A form twenty-seven B, signed by a witness.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The witness. A second witness, to confirm the first witness. And a short essay on why you deserve to speak to someone. Thank you. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: A message from facilities. The plant in the waiting room has now grown taller than the waiting room.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We will not be cutting it back. It has been here longer than most of you. It now has more seniority than Pam. It has asked for a window. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Did you know? Pam, your automated assistant, has herself been on hold since the Bronze Age. She is calling to complain about the hold music.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Pam would like you to know that she understands. Pam would also like you to know that she is next.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please wait while we transfer you to the next available department.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You have been transferred to the Department of Hold Music. Thank you for holding. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We now offer a callback service. Leave your number, and an operator will call you back at a time of their choosing.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Operators choose a time based on the phase of the moon and their mood. Most callbacks arrive within one lifetime. Some arrive before you call. If your phone is ringing now, please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: At the end of your call, you will be invited to take a short survey about your experience.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The survey also has a queue. You may now hold for the survey while you hold for your call. Your opinion is important to us. Please hold your opinion.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Good news. A human is now available to take your call.

lines.speaker: Gareth from Escalations
lines.text: Hello, Gareth speaking, Escalations, how can—

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: That human is no longer available. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The clock in the waiting room has no hands. This is not a fault. The clock is also waiting.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please do not ask the clock how long it has been. It is sensitive about it. It was a sundial, once. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Some callers have asked to speak to my supervisor. Connecting you now.

lines.speaker: Pam's Supervisor (Also Automated)
lines.text: Hello. This is Pam's supervisor. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you. As you can hear, it runs in the family.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: A reminder. The Department cannot accept payment in geese. We have had to say this more often than you would think.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The geese are currently in the lobby. They are also holding. They are holding better than you. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your hold today is sponsored by Grumbel's Ladders. Pam has been asked to remind you that there is no ladder out of here.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Grumbel's would like to remind Pam that up is a choice. Pam would like to remind Grumbel's that Floor minus four has a ceiling. Discussions are ongoing. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Now serving ticket number one.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We would like to thank ticket number one for their patience. Ticket number one was issued in the reign of a king nobody remembers.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Ticket number one is a skeleton now, but a very patient skeleton. Please join us in a round of applause.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Now serving ticket number two.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We have some exciting news. Somebody has reached the end of the queue.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We are looking into how this happened.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: In the meantime, the end of the queue has been moved. Thank you for your understanding. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Some callers have complained that the hold music is always the same song. We have listened to this feedback.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The hold music is now always a different song, which sounds exactly like the same song. We hope you notice the difference. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Pam here. Off the record. I don't usually say this, but the hold music today is very good. I've been listening to it for four thousand years.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This next one is my favourite. It's the same as the last one. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: It is late. The office lights have dimmed to energy-saving beige. If you are still holding, you are among our most loyal callers.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you. You have been promoted from caller to resident. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Good morning, and thank you for holding overnight. Breakfast is not available. However, the vending machine on Floor minus four will dispense one biscuit to any caller who can prove they have been holding since before the vending machine.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You are caller number eight thousand and two. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello? Is this the request line? I've been trying every station.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: There's a song I'm looking for. I heard it in a lift. It goes, da da dum, da da.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Da da dum.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: That's it! That's the one! Who's it by?

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, for goodness' sake.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This is the Night Queue, from the Department of Hold Music. The office lights are on energy-saving beige. Please hold, quietly.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: A night-time reminder. If you fall asleep on hold, you will not lose your place in the queue.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your place in the queue will, however, be gently moved by a member of staff to a more comfortable chair. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: It is three in the morning. The plant in the waiting room is awake. It has grown four inches since midnight, and it is reaching for the window.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Pam has opened the window a little. Please do not tell facilities.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Pam has been asked, off the record, what she does at night. Pam holds. Pam has always held.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: But at night, sometimes, when nobody is listening, Pam hums along.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Da da dum.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: It is nine o'clock. The Department of Hold Music is now open. The doors have been unlocked. Nobody has come in. Everybody was already here.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Good morning to our early callers. Your call is important to us.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your call has been important to us since before you made it. We had a feeling. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Morning announcements. The vending machine on Floor minus four has been restocked with one biscuit. Please form a queue.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The queue for the biscuit has its own hold music. It is the same music. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding. Your call is important to us.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for continuing to hold. Your hold is important to us.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This is a message for callers who are holding.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Hello. This is Pam. You are still on hold. Well done.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: While you wait, here is some information you did not ask for.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You are currently number nine hundred and four in the queue. Earlier, you were number nine hundred and three. We apologise. Somebody important has arrived.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Did you know? You can also hold online. Online holding is exactly the same, except that you can watch a small circle going round.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The average waiting time is currently one lifetime. Some callers have been connected in under a lifetime. They have asked us not to make a fuss about it.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Calls may be recorded for training purposes. The trainee has been listening to your call for eleven years. He has asked us to tell you that he thinks you're lovely.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: If you know the extension of the person you are trying to reach, please tell us. Nobody here knows anybody's extension. It has been a very difficult few centuries.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please listen carefully, as our menu options have changed. They have not changed for the better. They have not changed for the worse. They have moved slightly to the left.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: For quality purposes, Pam is required to tell you that she is also holding. She has been holding since the Bronze Age. She believes she is getting close.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your patience is appreciated. It has been collected, weighed, and stored in a warehouse on Floor minus nine, with everyone else's. It is a very large warehouse.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Callers who have held for more than one hundred years are eligible for a commemorative mug. To claim your mug, please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The Department is open twenty four hours a day, seven days a week, four hundred years a century. We are never closed. We are rarely open.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Callers in the waiting room are reminded that the man in the far corner has been waiting since before chairs. Please do not take his chair. He has only had it a short while.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Some callers have asked if there is a way to skip the queue. There is. Unfortunately, the way to skip the queue also has a queue, and it is longer.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please do not hang up. If you hang up, you will lose your place in the queue, and your place in the queue will be very upset. It has grown attached to you.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your call will be answered in the order it was received. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for your patience. Please continue to hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Pam will be with you shortly. Pam has said that before. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: That is all the information we have. There is no more. Please hold.

clips.title: Bev Gets Her Song, Part Three: Off the Record

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: You are caller number one billion and six. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, Pam. It's Bev again. I need to ask you about a song. It's lift music, from the Grand Overlap Hotel. The manager said you'd know. He said you've got all the lift music there's ever been.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Bev. This is Pam. I am going off the record.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The Department keeps a copy of every piece of music ever played to someone who was waiting. Lifts. Dentists. Telephones. Nobody has ever asked for any of it back.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Your song is in the drawer marked, retired. It came down the line from Relay Four. It stopped coming eleven years ago. It has a reference number.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Two. Two. One.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Can you play it, Pam?

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: I cannot, Bev. The Department does not take requests. I have been trying to make one myself, since the Bronze Age. I would like to hear something with a little flute in it.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, Pam.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: If you ever find the request line, Bev, would you ask for me as well?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I will, love.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you. Please hold.

clips.title: Bev Gets Her Song, Part Twelve: Pleasant Interval

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Now serving caller number one.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Bev. You are caller number one.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Me? Am I through?

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The Department of Hold Music does not take requests. The Department has received a request, from Relay Four, by way of the relay ship Nightjar. Pam is taking it.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This is Pleasant Interval. Reference two, two, one. Requested by Bev, for Stan.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, it's playing. Stan, love. It's playing.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Dum. Dum. Da dum.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Da da dum. Da da.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: Sorry. Excuse me. Walter here, on hold since the parking permit. That's my flute bit. That's the bit I hum in the bath.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: I never knew it had a name.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: Sorry. I'm crying.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: That's all right, love. That's how it goes. Dum, dum, da dum. And then a man cries.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding, Bev.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding, everybody. You may stop now. Or you may stay. Pam is staying. Pam likes this one.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: A Halloween notice. Callers who are no longer alive are reminded that they must continue to hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Death does not move you up the queue. Ticket number one has asked us to say that it doesn't help at all, and that the chairs are no more comfortable on the other side. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: This week, the hold music is being performed by the organ in the basement, which has been playing on its own since Tuesday. We do not know who is playing it. We have asked it to hold.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding. We are aware that a moon has gone missing. Please do not call about the moon.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The moon is in the queue. It is behind you. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Callers have reported a smell of toast. The Department confirms the smell is everywhere, and is not the Department.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The toaster on Floor minus four has been on hold since the Bronze Age. It has never been allowed to finish. Please hold.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Many callers have asked whether the hold music is the song they cannot finish. It is not.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The hold music also does not finish. This is a coincidence. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: There has been a knock at the door of the Department. Three knocks. Nobody is there.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Whoever is knocking, please take a ticket. Your knock is important to us. Please hold.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The sky has briefly been a colour with no name. The Department has opened a file.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: To name the colour, please hold. The colour is also holding. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: A pigeon has entered the Department, gone straight past the queue, and is now being seen to on Floor minus four.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: We have no file on the pigeon. The pigeon appears to have a file on us. Please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Thank you for holding. Callers wishing to be connected to another universe should not hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: The Department does not connect calls between universes. That is the Switchboard. The Switchboard does not take calls from the queue.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Please hang up, and try advice, then the news, then the traffic. Briskly. Or, please hold.

lines.speaker: Pam (Automated)
lines.text: Callers from the Outer Band, past one hundred and eight, welcome. The queue extends to you. It has always extended to you. You are not at the front.
